title: The pyramid, taken apart
sub: Data architecture, a series on what DAMA calls data architecture, between the business and the systems: the famous pyramid of data, information, knowledge and wisdom, what it gets right and what it gets wrong, and Inés Duarte's redrawing of it with arrows both ways, from a decision down to the records and back up to a person who decides.
howto: Glass in the layers' colours is the confirmed model: gold is the business layer, peach the information layer, where data architecture works. The pyramid is drawn in glass, one colour for each level. A line down on the left is what asks; a line up on the right is what answers. Chile in 1972 is drawn in lamp-light: the telex, the factories, and the software's warnings, each beside its factory's normal band.
